root_cause.text: The BPF program signature verification path in `bpf_prog_verify_signature()` accepted an unbounded user-controlled `attr->signature_size`, allowing oversized signature allocations to fall into expensive `kmalloc_large`/`vmalloc` paths in the BPF syscall subsystem.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early check in `kernel/bpf/syscall.c` rejecting `attr->signature_size > KMALLOC_MAX_CACHE_SIZE` with `-EINVAL`, and the commit message explicitly says larger sizes “open the door for abuse by passing excessive size values and forcing the kernel into expensive allocation paths (via kmalloc_large or vmalloc).”

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject oversized BPF signatures early to avoid large allocations and enforce a practical signature size limit.
intent_record.what: A size check was added at the start of bpf_prog_verify_signature(): if attr->signature_size is greater than KMALLOC_MAX_CACHE_SIZE, the function now returns -EINVAL before attempting any keyring lookup or signature allocation. A comment was also added explaining that kmalloc_large/vmalloc should not be used for signatures.
intent_record.how: At runtime, oversized BPF program signatures are now rejected immediately instead of proceeding to allocation paths that might use large allocations or vmalloc. This prevents the verifier from handling signature buffers beyond the intended practical limit and fails early with an invalid argument error.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet clearly shows the vulnerable signature-verification path and it does not impose any bound on the user-controlled signature size. In `bpf_prog_verify_signature()`, the code directly uses `attr->signature_size` in `kvmemdup_bpfptr(usig, attr->signature_size);` and then again in `bpf_dynptr_init(&sig_ptr, sig, ..., attr->signature_size);`. There is no length check, maximum cap, or validation before allocating/copying the signature buffer. That matches the root cause: an unbounded `attr->signature_size` can drive oversized `kmalloc_large`/`vmalloc`-backed allocations in the BPF syscall path. The fix is not present in this function body because it contains no restriction on `signature_size`; it only checks key lookup and errors from `kvmemdup_bpfptr`.
